Author, born at Troyes on 2 June 1901, died at Geneva on 6 January 1982; elected full member of SACEM on 27 April 1928; administrator of SACEM, vice-president and secretary general of the SDRM; Prix Albert Willemetz, 1946.

sources.researchNote: Besides the dates, the register records the offices he later held in the society and in the mechanical rights body, which no other record consulted for him mentions.

media.altText: Halftone portrait of the lyricist Louis Poterat in round spectacles.
media.description: The clipping retains the printed caption below the portrait — “Louis POTERAT / que vous entendrez aujourd’hui à 14 h.” — because it identifies the sitter.
media.publicCaption: Louis Poterat, who wrote the French lyrics of Le plus petit baiser and À Paris tiguidiguidi in 1933 and of Amanda and C’est ton amour in 1934. The portrait is later: it announced a broadcast in the Paris radio weekly Les Ondes on 20 July 1941.
media.publicCreditLine: Photographer unidentified; Les Ondes (Paris), 20 July 1941; digitised issue at World Radio History.
media.rightsNote: Reuse rights are not cleared. The photograph appeared in a French magazine in July 1941 and no photographer is credited. Even read as an anonymous work, its French term of seventy years from publication was still running on 1 January 1996, the United States restoration date, so the URAA restored United States copyright; if the photographer were identified, the term would run from their death instead. The digitising site presents the issue as a scanned periodical and grants no licence. A reduced-resolution reproduction (420 × 541 px, from 1297 × 1672 px) is used here for scholarly identification of a documented Kaper collaborator.
media.title: Louis Poterat — Les Ondes, 20 July 1941
